questions.q: What does calling robot.indexer.feed() actually do?
questions.correct: Records that we want feeding; update() moves the servo
wrong: Spins the indexer servo for exactly one second
Moves the servo right away, without any update() call
Waits until a pollen is loaded, then feeds it out
questions.explain: feed() only flips the feeding flag. The servo's power is set in update(), so nothing moves until robot.update() runs.

questions.q: What does robot.update() do?
questions.correct: Calls update() on every subsystem so hardware matches its state
wrong: Downloads the newest version of your code to the robot
Resets every subsystem back to off
Refreshes the telemetry shown on the Driver Hub
questions.explain: robot.update() is the scheduler: it walks the list of subsystems and calls each one's update(), which turns their state into real motor and servo power.

questions.q: An auto calls robot.flywheel.toggle(); and then sleep(3000);. What does the flywheel do during those 3 seconds?
questions.correct: Nothing, because update() never runs during the sleep
wrong: Spins up to its target RPM, ready to shoot
Spins at half speed until the sleep finishes
Turns on and off over and over, once per second
questions.explain: toggle() only records the wish. The flywheel's power is set in update(), and nothing calls update() while the OpMode is asleep.

questions.q: During a long sleep() in an auto, what happens to follower.update()?
questions.correct: It isn't called, so nothing holds the robot on its spot
wrong: It keeps running in the background, holding the robot still
It runs twice as often to make up for the pause
It drives the robot back to its starting pose
questions.explain: sleep() pauses the whole OpMode. follower.update() is what holds the robot at the end of its path, and it can't run while the OpMode sleeps.

questions.q: Why is sleep(20) inside a loop OK, when sleep(3000) on its own is not?
questions.correct: The loop still calls update() every lap; the short pause only sets the pace
wrong: sleep(20) is too short for the robot to notice at all
Short sleeps are run on a separate, faster thread
It's not OK either; any sleep() freezes the robot for the match
questions.explain: A tiny pause between laps keeps the heartbeat going: update() still runs every lap, about 50 times a second.

questions.q: How long does this loop take?  for (int i = 0; i < 150 && opModeIsActive(); i++) { ... sleep(20); }
questions.correct: About 3 seconds
wrong: About 150 seconds
About 20 seconds
About 0.15 seconds
questions.explain: 150 laps × 20 ms per lap = 3000 ms = about 3 seconds.

questions.q: Each lap of your loop takes about 20 ms. How many laps keep the heartbeat going for 5 seconds?
questions.correct: 250 laps
wrong: 100 laps
500 laps
5 laps
questions.explain: 5 seconds = 5000 ms, and 5000 ÷ 20 = 250 laps.

questions.q: In  for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++), what does i++ do?
questions.correct: Adds 1 to the lap counter after each lap
wrong: Doubles the lap counter every single lap
Starts a second loop inside the first one
Ends the loop as soon as it is reached
questions.explain: A for loop has three parts: start (int i = 0), keep going while (i < 150), and after each lap (i++), which adds 1.

questions.q: Why can two of these for loops, one after the other, both use int i?
questions.correct: Each i only exists inside its own loop
wrong: Java renames the second i to j behind the scenes
The second loop deletes the first loop's i before it starts
They can't; the second one will always fail to compile
questions.explain: A variable declared in a for loop's parentheses only lives inside that loop, so each loop gets its own fresh i.

questions.q: When does opModeIsActive() become false?
questions.correct: When STOP is pressed or the AUTO period ends
wrong: As soon as the robot finishes its first path
Whenever the flywheel reaches its target speed
When the battery voltage drops below 12 volts
questions.explain: opModeIsActive() is true while the OpMode is running and turns false on STOP or when the 30-second AUTO ends.

questions.q: What could happen if a waiting loop leaves out opModeIsActive()?
questions.correct: The robot ignores STOP until the loop finishes counting
wrong: The loop runs twice as fast as it should
The flywheel can never reach its target speed
The code compiles, but the loop is skipped entirely
questions.explain: Without opModeIsActive() in the condition, the loop keeps going after STOP is pressed. Every loop should listen for STOP.

questions.q: In the condition  i < 150 && opModeIsActive(), what does && mean?
questions.correct: Both parts must be true to keep looping
wrong: Either part being true keeps the loop going
Run the left part first, then the right part on the next lap
Compare the two parts to see if they are equal
questions.explain: && means AND: the loop continues only while it hasn't finished its laps AND the OpMode is still active.

questions.q: What does follower.update() do while the robot waits at the end of a path?
questions.correct: Keeps nudging the robot back onto its spot
wrong: Spins the flywheel up to its target speed
Plans the next path in the background
Saves the robot's position to a file
questions.explain: Paths are followed with holdEnd = true, so each follower.update() at the end of a path pushes the robot back to its end point.

questions.q: In Path Capture, what does pressing X at the shooting spot do?
questions.correct: Adds a bookmark in the code where you write the action
wrong: Makes the robot shoot automatically when the auto runs
Saves the auto file and closes the Path Capture tool
Records the shooter's exact speed at that point on the field
questions.explain: A button press only inserts a CAP:ACTION / CAP:ACTION-END pair of comments. The robot does nothing there until you write the code.

questions.q: Where does your shooting code go in a captured auto?
questions.correct: Between the CAP:ACTION and CAP:ACTION-END lines
wrong: Above the @Autonomous line at the very top of the file
Inside the path-following while loop after chain 1
In a brand new Shoot.java file in your package
questions.explain: The action block marks the spot in the auto. Code between the two CAP lines runs there, and is kept when you reopen the file in Path Capture.

questions.q: Why must both CAP lines stay exactly as Path Capture wrote them?
questions.correct: Path Capture needs them to reopen your auto for editing
wrong: The robot reads them to decide which button to press
Java won't compile a file without those two comments
They tell the flywheel which speed it should hold
questions.explain: They're comments, so Java ignores them, but Path Capture uses them to reload the file. If one is changed or deleted, it refuses to load it.

questions.q: After the action block finishes, what does a captured auto do next?
questions.correct: Carries on with the next path, for example to park
wrong: Stops the OpMode, since the action was the last step
Goes back to the start pose and repeats the action
Waits for the driver to press X again before moving
questions.explain: The auto runs in order: follow a path, run the action, then follow the next path you captured.

questions.q: AUTO lasts 30 seconds. A shot uses about 3 s to spin up and 5 s to feed. How much time is left to drive?
questions.correct: About 22 seconds
wrong: About 8 seconds
About 27 seconds
About 15 seconds
questions.explain: 3 + 5 = 8 seconds for the shot, so about 30 − 8 = 22 seconds remain to drive to the shooting spot and on to park.

questions.q: In an auto, what is robot.indexer.feed() the same as in TeleOp?
questions.correct: Holding down the X button
wrong: Pressing Y to toggle the flywheel
Pressing A to turn the intake on
Moving the right stick to trim the speed
questions.explain: In TeleOp, holding X calls robot.indexer.feed() every loop. In an auto there's no driver, so the code calls it directly.

questions.q: Why does the shooting code call robot.update() one last time after turning everything off?
questions.correct: So the flywheel and indexer actually stop right away
wrong: To make the robot drive to the parking spot
To save the auto before the match ends
To reset the lap counter back to zero
questions.explain: toggle() and stop() only record the wishes. One more robot.update() applies them, so the motors stop immediately.
